sources.staff: Wikipedia: List of current NFL head coaches / offensive coordinators / defensive coordinators (read 2026-09-19); head coaches cross-checked against ESPN's team API
sources.records: Wikipedia head-coach list (regular season W-L-T, playoff W-L) as of 2026-09-19; refreshed by the pipeline from the schedule for the current tenure
sources.photos: Wikimedia Commons, each with its own licence and credit; no photo means none is available under an open licence
sources.bios: Written for this site from the coaches' Wikipedia articles; one or two sentences of background, no claims about play-calling

notes: Edit this file by hand when a staff changes mid-season. The pipeline flags a head coach whose name no longer matches ESPN's.

HC.name: Mike LaFleur
HC.bio: First-year head coach after three seasons running the Rams offense as coordinator (2023 to 2025); earlier stops as an assistant with the 49ers, Jets and Falcons.

OC.name: Nathaniel Hackett
OC.bio: Former Packers and Jaguars offensive coordinator and Broncos head coach (2022); spent 2025 as an analyst in Green Bay before taking over the Cardinals offense.

DC.name: Nick Rallis
DC.bio: In his fourth season running the Cardinals defense, now under a new head coach; came from the Eagles' linebackers room and played at Minnesota.

HC.name: Kevin Stefanski
HC.bio: Head coach of the Browns from 2020 to 2025, twice named Coach of the Year there; a former Penn safety who came up through the Vikings' offensive staff.

OC.name: Tommy Rees
OC.bio: Followed Stefanski from Cleveland, where he was offensive coordinator in 2025; a former Notre Dame quarterback and Alabama offensive coordinator.

DC.name: Jeff Ulbrich
DC.bio: Second season running the Falcons defense after four as the Jets' coordinator (and their interim head coach in 2024); a former 49ers linebacker.

HC.name: Jesse Minter
HC.bio: First-year head coach, back in Baltimore where he was an assistant from 2017 to 2020; ran the Chargers defense in 2024 and 2025 and Michigan's national-title defense before that.

OC.name: Declan Doyle
OC.bio: Thirty-year-old coordinator who ran the Bears offense in 2025 under Ben Johnson; started as a Saints offensive assistant and coached tight ends in Denver.

DC.name: Anthony Weaver
DC.bio: Former Ravens defensive lineman who ran the Dolphins defense the last two seasons; earlier assistant stops with the Jets, Bills, Browns and Texans.

HC.name: Joe Brady
HC.bio: Promoted from within after two seasons as the Bills' offensive coordinator; won the Broyles Award as LSU's passing-game coordinator in 2019 and was Carolina's coordinator before Buffalo.

OC.name: Pete Carmichael Jr.
OC.bio: Eighteen seasons on the Saints' offensive staff, fifteen of them as coordinator under Sean Payton, then two years as a senior assistant in Denver.

DC.name: Jim Leonhard
DC.prev: Denver Broncos assistant head coach & defensive pass game coordinator (2025)
DC.bio: Ten-year NFL safety turned coach; Wisconsin's defensive coordinator and interim head coach before joining Denver's staff, now in his first season running the Bills defense.

HC.name: Dave Canales
HC.bio: Third season in Carolina after a long run on Pete Carroll's Seattle staff and one year as Tampa Bay's offensive coordinator; took the Panthers to the playoffs in 2025.

OC.name: Brad Idzik
OC.prev: Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receivers coach (2023)
OC.bio: Came with Canales from Tampa Bay, where he coached receivers; now in his third season as coordinator.

DC.name: Ejiro Evero
DC.bio: Fourth season running the Panthers defense after one as Denver's coordinator; earlier an assistant with the Rams, Packers and Buccaneers.

HC.name: Ben Johnson
HC.bio: Built top-five offenses in three seasons as Detroit's coordinator, then went 11-6 with a playoff win in his first year in Chicago, the Bears' first postseason victory since 2010.

OC.name: Press Taylor
OC.bio: Promoted after a season as passing-game coordinator; previously Jacksonville's offensive coordinator and a long-time Eagles assistant.

DC.name: Dennis Allen
DC.bio: Second season with the Bears after head-coaching stints with the Raiders and Saints; spent most of the 2010s running the Saints defense.

photo.artist: All-Pro Reels from District of Columbia, USA

HC.name: Zac Taylor
HC.bio: Eighth season in Cincinnati; after a 6-25-1 start he took the Bengals to Super Bowl LVI and an AFC title game, and his five playoff wins match the franchise's total before he arrived.

OC.name: Dan Pitcher
OC.bio: A Bengals assistant since 2016 and Joe Burrow's position coach for four years before taking the coordinator job; a former Colgate and SUNY Cortland quarterback.

DC.name: Al Golden
DC.prev: Notre Dame Fighting Irish defensive coordinator (2022-2024)
DC.bio: Former Temple and Miami head coach who returned to the Bengals after running Notre Dame's defense; second season as coordinator.

HC.name: Todd Monken
HC.bio: First NFL head-coaching job at 60 after running the Ravens offense and Georgia's two national-title offenses; was Southern Miss head coach from 2013 to 2015.

OC.name: Travis Switzer
OC.bio: Followed Monken from Baltimore, where he coordinated the run game; a former Akron offensive lineman in his first coordinator job.

DC.name: Mike Rutenberg
DC.prev: Atlanta Falcons defensive pass game coordinator (2025)
DC.bio: First season as an NFL coordinator after coordinating the Falcons' pass defense; earlier college stops at UCLA and New Mexico.

HC.name: Brian Schottenheimer
HC.bio: Second season after being promoted from Cowboys offensive coordinator; a coordinator for the Jets, Rams and Seahawks over two decades before that.

OC.name: Klayton Adams
OC.bio: Offensive-line coach by trade (Cardinals, Colorado, Stanford) in his second season as coordinator.

DC.name: Christian Parker
DC.prev: Philadelphia Eagles defensive backs coach & pass game coordinator (2024-2025)
DC.bio: Coached the secondary on Philadelphia's Super Bowl LIX defense; first season running a defense at 34.

HC.name: Sean Payton
HC.bio: Fourth season in Denver after sixteen with the Saints, where he won Super Bowl XLIV and whose offenses scored more points than any other coach's over that span.

OC.name: Davis Webb
OC.prev: Broncos quarterbacks coach & pass game coordinator (2025)
OC.bio: A 2017 Giants draft pick as a quarterback, retired into coaching and became Bo Nix's position coach; promoted to coordinator at 31.

DC.name: Vance Joseph
DC.bio: Fourth season back in Denver, where he was head coach in 2017 and 2018; ran the Cardinals defense for four years in between.

photo.artist: Army Sgt. Zach Sheely of the Colorado National Guard

HC.name: Dan Campbell
HC.bio: Sixth season; an eleven-year NFL tight end who took the Lions to their first division title since 1993 and an NFC title game in 2023.

OC.name: Drew Petzing
OC.bio: Ran the Cardinals offense for three seasons; earlier on Kevin Stefanski's staffs in Minnesota and Cleveland.

DC.name: Kelvin Sheppard
DC.bio: Eight-year NFL linebacker promoted from the Lions' linebackers room after Aaron Glenn left; second season as coordinator.

HC.name: Matt LaFleur
HC.bio: Eighth season in Green Bay; a former Rams and Titans offensive coordinator, and the Packers have had a winning record in every one of his seasons.

OC.name: Adam Stenavich
OC.prev: Packers offensive line coach & run game coordinator (2019-2021)
OC.bio: Fifth season as coordinator after coaching the Packers' offensive line; a former NFL offensive tackle.

DC.name: Jonathan Gannon
DC.bio: Head coach of the Cardinals for three seasons and, before that, the coordinator of the Eagles' Super Bowl LVII defense; first season in Green Bay.

HC.name: DeMeco Ryans
HC.bio: Fourth season; a two-time Pro Bowl linebacker for the Texans who was Assistant Coach of the Year running the 49ers defense in 2022.

OC.name: Nick Caley
OC.prev: Los Angeles Rams tight ends coach & pass game coordinator (2024)
OC.bio: Second season as coordinator after a decade in college and tight-ends jobs with the Patriots and Rams.

DC.name: Matt Burke
DC.bio: Fourth season running the Texans defense under Ryans; previously Miami's coordinator and the Eagles' run-game coordinator.

HC.name: Shane Steichen
HC.bio: Fourth season; coordinated the Eagles' Super Bowl LVII offense and the Chargers' before that.

OC.name: Jim Bob Cooter
OC.bio: Fourth season in Indianapolis; ran the Lions offense from 2015 to 2018 and coached Jets running backs before that.

DC.name: Lou Anarumo
DC.bio: Six seasons running the Bengals defense, including the Super Bowl LVI run; second season with the Colts.

HC.name: Liam Coen
HC.bio: Went 13-4 in his first season after coordinating Tampa Bay's offense in 2024 and the Rams' in 2022; a Kentucky offensive coordinator in between.

OC.name: Grant Udinski
OC.prev: Minnesota Vikings assistant offensive coordinator/quarterbacks coach (2024)
OC.bio: Thirty-year-old coordinator in his second season, hired from Kevin O'Connell's Vikings staff.

DC.name: Anthony Campanile
DC.prev: Green Bay Packers linebackers coach & run game coordinator (2024)
DC.bio: Second season running the Jaguars defense after coaching linebackers in Green Bay and Miami.

HC.name: Andy Reid
HC.bio: Fourteenth season in Kansas City and the league's longest-tenured coach; three Super Bowl titles with the Chiefs after fourteen years running the Eagles.

OC.name: Eric Bieniemy
OC.bio: Back for a second stint as Chiefs coordinator, the job he held for the 2019 and 2022 title seasons; Colorado's all-time leading rusher as a player.

DC.name: Steve Spagnuolo
DC.bio: Eighth season with the Chiefs and the coordinator of all three of their title defenses; earlier ran the Giants' Super Bowl XLII defense and was the Rams' head coach.

HC.name: Sean McVay
HC.bio: Tenth season; the youngest head coach to win a Super Bowl (LVI) and Coach of the Year, hired at 30 after coordinating Washington's offense.

OC.name: Nathan Scheelhaase
OC.bio: Promoted from passing-game coordinator; a former Illinois quarterback who was Iowa State's offensive coordinator before joining the Rams.

DC.name: Chris Shula
DC.prev: Los Angeles Rams linebackers coach & pass rush coordinator (2023)
DC.bio: Third season running the Rams defense after coaching their linebackers and pass rush; grandson of Don Shula.

HC.name: Jim Harbaugh
HC.bio: Third season with the Chargers; won a national title at Michigan and took the 49ers to Super Bowl XLVII, after fourteen years as an NFL quarterback.

OC.name: Mike McDaniel
OC.bio: Head coach of the Dolphins for four seasons and the 49ers' offensive coordinator before that; first season calling the Chargers offense.

DC.name: Chris O'Leary
DC.prev: Western Michigan Broncos defensive coordinator & safeties coach (2025)
DC.bio: Thirty-four-year-old coordinator hired from Western Michigan, where he ran the defense and coached safeties in 2025; first NFL coordinator job.

HC.name: Klint Kubiak
HC.bio: First-year head coach after coordinating Seattle's Super Bowl LX offense; earlier the Saints' and Vikings' offensive coordinator, and Gary Kubiak's son.

OC.name: Andrew Janocko
OC.bio: Followed Kubiak from Seattle, where he coached quarterbacks on the title team; a former Pitt quarterback.

DC.name: Rob Leonard
DC.prev: Las Vegas Raiders defensive line coach & run game coordinator (2023-2025)
DC.bio: Promoted from the Raiders' defensive-line room, where he also coordinated the run defense for three seasons; first season as coordinator.

HC.name: Jeff Hafley
HC.bio: First NFL head-coaching job; ran the Packers defense the last two seasons and was Boston College's head coach from 2020 to 2023.

OC.name: Bobby Slowik
OC.bio: Houston's offensive coordinator for C.J. Stroud's first two seasons, then a year on the Dolphins staff before taking over the offense.

DC.name: Sean Duggan
DC.bio: Thirty-three-year-old coordinator who came with Hafley from Green Bay, where he coached linebackers.

HC.name: Kevin O'Connell
HC.bio: Fifth season; coordinated the Rams' Super Bowl LVI offense and was 2024 Coach of the Year after a 14-3 season with Sam Darnold.

OC.name: Wes Phillips
OC.prev: Los Angeles Rams tight ends coach & passing game coordinator (2019-2021)
OC.bio: Fifth season as O'Connell's coordinator after three years on the Rams staff; son of Wade Phillips.

DC.name: Brian Flores
DC.prev: Pittsburgh Steelers senior defensive assistant & linebackers coach (2022)
DC.bio: Fourth season running the Vikings defense; head coach of the Dolphins from 2019 to 2021 after eleven years on the Patriots staff.

HC.name: Mike Vrabel
HC.bio: Went 14-3 in his first season back in New England, where he won three Super Bowls as a linebacker; head coach of the Titans from 2018 to 2023.

OC.name: Josh McDaniels
OC.bio: Fifteenth non-consecutive season as Patriots coordinator, with head-coaching stints in Denver and Las Vegas in between.

DC.name: Zak Kuhr
DC.prev: New England Patriots inside linebackers coach (2025)
DC.bio: Promoted from inside linebackers coach; a Florida graduate with college and NFL stops before New England, in his first season as a coordinator.

HC.name: Kellen Moore
HC.bio: Second season; coordinated the Eagles' Super Bowl LIX offense and the Cowboys' and Chargers' before that, after a career as a backup quarterback.

OC.name: Doug Nussmeier
OC.bio: Second season as Moore's coordinator after coaching quarterbacks for him in Philadelphia and Dallas; a former Idaho and NFL quarterback.

photo.artist: BU Rob13 derivative work; original work by Brad Muckenthaler

DC.name: Brandon Staley
DC.bio: Second season running the Saints defense; head coach of the Chargers from 2021 to 2023 and coordinator of the Rams' top-ranked 2020 defense.

HC.name: John Harbaugh
HC.bio: First season with the Giants after eighteen in Baltimore, where he won Super Bowl XLVII and 193 games including playoffs.

OC.name: Matt Nagy
OC.bio: Three seasons as the Chiefs' coordinator and four as Bears head coach (Coach of the Year in 2018); first season with the Giants.

DC.name: Dennard Wilson
DC.bio: Ran the Titans defense for two seasons; a former NFL safety and long-time secondary coach (Rams, Jets, Eagles, Ravens).

HC.name: Aaron Glenn
HC.bio: Second season after a 3-14 debut; coordinated the Lions defense for four years and played fifteen NFL seasons at cornerback, eight of them for the Jets.

OC.name: Frank Reich
OC.bio: Former Colts and Panthers head coach and the Eagles' Super Bowl LII coordinator; spent 2025 as Stanford's interim head coach.

DC.name: Brian Duker
DC.prev: Miami Dolphins secondary coach & pass game coordinator (2024-2025)
DC.bio: First season as a coordinator after coaching Miami's secondary; a Towson graduate who started in the Lions' quality-control ranks.

HC.name: Nick Sirianni
HC.bio: Sixth season; playoffs in each of his first five, two NFC titles and the Super Bowl LIX win, after coordinating the Colts offense.

OC.name: Sean Mannion
OC.bio: Thirty-four-year-old former NFL backup quarterback, promoted to coordinator after one season coaching Green Bay's quarterbacks.

DC.name: Vic Fangio
DC.bio: Third season with the Eagles and the coordinator of their Super Bowl LIX defense; more than thirty NFL seasons including three as Broncos head coach.

HC.name: Mike McCarthy
HC.bio: First season with his hometown Steelers after nineteen as a head coach in Green Bay and Dallas, including the Packers' Super Bowl XLV win.

OC.name: Brian Angelichio
OC.prev: Minnesota Vikings tight ends coach & pass game coordinator (2022-2025)
OC.bio: First season as a coordinator after four years coaching tight ends and the passing game in Minnesota.

DC.name: Patrick Graham
DC.bio: Four seasons running the Raiders defense and two the Giants'; first season in Pittsburgh.

HC.name: Mike Macdonald
HC.bio: Third season; won Super Bowl LX in his second year after building the Ravens' top-ranked 2023 defense as coordinator.

OC.name: Brian Fleury
OC.prev: San Francisco 49ers tight ends coach & run game coordinator (2022-2025)
OC.bio: Hired from Kyle Shanahan's staff, where he coached tight ends and the run game for four seasons; first season as a coordinator.

DC.name: Aden Durde
DC.bio: Third season running the Seahawks defense, the league's best in 2025; a British former linebacker who coached the Cowboys' defensive line.

HC.name: Kyle Shanahan
HC.bio: Tenth season; four NFC title games and two Super Bowl appearances with the 49ers after coordinating Atlanta's 2016 league-best offense.

OC.name: Klay Kubiak
OC.bio: Second season as coordinator on Shanahan's staff; a former Colorado State quarterback and Gary Kubiak's son.

DC.name: Raheem Morris
DC.bio: Back as a coordinator after two seasons as Falcons head coach; ran the Rams' Super Bowl LVI defense and was Tampa Bay's head coach from 2009 to 2011.

HC.name: Todd Bowles
HC.bio: Fifth season as head coach and still the Buccaneers' defensive play-caller, a role he has held since 2019; head coach of the Jets from 2015 to 2018.

OC.name: Zac Robinson
OC.bio: Two seasons as Atlanta's coordinator after five on Sean McVay's Rams staff; a former Oklahoma State quarterback.

DC.name: Todd Bowles
DC.bio: The head coach runs the defense himself, as he has since arriving as coordinator in 2019 for the Super Bowl LV season.

HC.name: Robert Saleh
HC.bio: First season in Tennessee after a year back as the 49ers' defensive coordinator; head coach of the Jets from 2021 to 2024.

OC.name: Brian Daboll
OC.bio: Giants head coach for four seasons (Coach of the Year in 2022) and the coordinator who built Buffalo's offense around Josh Allen; first season with the Titans.

DC.name: Gus Bradley
DC.bio: The original architect of Seattle's Legion of Boom defense, Jaguars head coach from 2013 to 2016 and a coordinator for the Chargers and Colts since; first season in Tennessee.

HC.name: Dan Quinn
HC.bio: Third season in Washington, which he took to the NFC title game in his first year; head coach of the Falcons from 2015 to 2020 and coordinator of Seattle's Super Bowl defenses.

OC.name: David Blough
OC.bio: Thirty-one-year-old former NFL quarterback promoted after two seasons as an assistant quarterbacks coach; first season as a coordinator.

DC.name: Daronte Jones
DC.prev: Minnesota Vikings defensive backs coach & pass game coordinator (2022-2025)
DC.bio: Four seasons coaching Minnesota's secondary under Brian Flores; earlier LSU's defensive coordinator. First season running an NFL defense.
